citation.title: LETTER: 225+ Organizations demand COP30 center people, not polluters
citation.type: advocacy open letter (web page), endorsed by 225+ organisations

question: Argues that the COP30 Presidency should not invite corporations, especially fossil fuel and other high-emitting industries, into the climate talks without safeguards, and asks for a polluter-free COP, a polluter-free Presidency and an Accountability Framework. It does not study delegations.

definitions.definition: Not defined. The letter states that the UNFCCC has no agreed definition.
definitions.quote: It does not even have an agreed definition of what a “conflict of interest” is, let alone any measures on how to address one.
definitions.page: In his 7th letter to the international community (para 4)

definitions.definition: Used as a broad label for fossil fuel and other big polluting industries and their enablers. No criteria are given for which firms count.
definitions.quote: polluting businesses, and their enablers, are directly responsible for the climate crisis
definitions.page: In his 7th letter to the international community (para 2)

definitions.definition: A Presidency where people with close ties to or affiliations with polluters hold no leadership role.
definitions.quote: Committing to a polluter-free Presidency where those with close ties to or affiliations with polluters have no role in the leadership of the climate talks.
definitions.page: In his 7th letter to the international community (para 7)

proxies.concept: fossil fuel link of a PR firm
proxies.indicator: The firm is said to have fossil fuel clients (Edelman, the COP30 media partner).
proxies.quote: a PR firm that actively has fossil fuel clientele
proxies.page: In his 7th letter to the international community (para 7)

findings.claim: The letter says corporate interests, particularly fossil fuel and other big polluting industries, have undermined climate action through lobbying and disinformation (assertion, no data given in the text).
findings.quote: corporate interests – particularly from the fossil fuel and other big polluting industries – have sabotaged climate progress through aggressive lobbying, disinformation, and glossy PR campaigns
findings.page: In his 7th letter to the international community (para 1)

findings.claim: The COP30 team's PR contractor is said to also promote major oil and gas companies.
findings.quote: the COP30 team has made a deal with a PR company that is simultaneously promoting the interests of major oil and gas companies
findings.page: In his 7th letter to the international community (para 1)

findings.claim: The UNFCCC is said to have no meaningful measures against private, vested interests; transparency requirements were strengthened from COP30 but are said not to amount to accountability.
findings.quote: transparency is a far cry from accountability.
findings.page: In his 7th letter to the international community (para 4)

findings.claim: Recommendation (not a finding): establish an Accountability Framework against corporate interference, especially from fossil fuel and high-emitting industries.
findings.quote: must prioritize the establishment of a strong Accountability Framework to protect against corporate interference and those with vested interests
findings.page: In his 7th letter to the international community (para 5)

findings.claim: Transparency International is listed among the endorsing organisations (the list is also headed by 225+ organisations; the Conflict of Interest Working Group of YOUNGO is also listed).
findings.quote: Endorsed by the following 225+ organizations and networks:
findings.page: In his 7th letter to the international community (para 11)

limitations.point: Advocacy letter: no data, no counts of business or fossil fuel delegates, no method for identifying or classifying them, no delegation or badge analysis.
Terms such as polluter, enabler, fossil fuel insider and corporate capture are used without operational definitions or criteria.
No author names or publication date on the extracted page; year 2025 inferred from the COP30 context and linked 2025 URLs, not stated in the text.
Claims rest on linked sources (news articles, UN documents) that were not read here.
